rows.brief: Performance, shippable core = PERF-2 + PERF-3 (plan names: PERF-1 harness + WOFF cache · PERF-2 render scheduling + debounce · PERF-3 deferred save + skip no-op renders · PERF-4 editor commits + colour pickers · PERF-5 pdf.js paint + chunk split · PERF-6 PDF in a Web Worker; the plan file itself is not in the repo). (a) While the user types continuously, the preview repaints at a bounded interval — give the render debounce a max-wait (e.g. a render at the latest ~1–1.5 s into a burst of edits) instead of freezing until typing stops (src/components/PdfPreview.jsx ~16, ~111). Keep the stale-render drop, the zoom repaint, the hidden-preview pause and error/Retry mechanics; tests/pdf/90-preview-mechanics.test.mjs and 90-preview-canvas-memory.test.mjs must still pass — extend 90-preview-mechanics (or a new 97- file on tests/pdf/preview-stub.mjs) with a continuous-typing case that fails today. (b) The store stops JSON-stringifying the whole app state into localStorage on every keystroke (src/hooks/useResumeStore.js ~111): coalesce saves (a short debounce, ≤ 300 ms, so Cypress assertions that read localStorage — they retry for 4 s — still pass) with a guaranteed synchronous flush on pagehide, visibilitychange→hidden and beforeunload, before sign-out / leave (cloudSyncLeave), before anything that reads the saved state back (cloud sync, backups, another tab's storage-event path) — no edit may ever be lost; and skip a save/render when the data is unchanged (no-op). All existing store/storage tests must still pass: grep tests/ for useResumeStore, storage-recovery, local-deletions, sign-out-leave, 18-cloud-sync, demo-seed, storage-backup and run them on CI, plus the Cypress specs that read localStorage right after an action (grep cypress/e2e for localStorage / cpwtcv). A fail-first test for each of (a) and (b). Remaining (report it): PERF-1, PERF-4, PERF-5, PERF-6.

Add a Page size control (A4 / US Letter) in Design — in the page/margins area (a 'Page' row or small section beside the margins control; read DesignPanel.jsx and where margins live). It writes settings.pageSize through the store's normal settings update, with the ids in src/constants/pageSize.js (PAGE_SIZES, PAGE_SIZE_IDS). Labels like 'A4 · 210 × 297 mm' and 'US Letter · 8.5 × 11 in', a SegmentControl-style choice with the current one selected. The default stays exactly what an unset pageSize prints today (existing résumés don't change size). Confirm every consumer honours it: the résumé PDF (page box), the preview (PdfPreview/EditorPreviewPane page dims), Word (page size and margins), the cover-letter PDF and Word, the dashboard thumbnails if they size pages; Markdown/ATS text are unaffected. Register the control in the parity registry (tests/pdf/parity/registry-design.mjs or its neighbour) with a measure (the PDF's page width/height changes to the chosen size) — 00-registry fails for an unmeasured control. Fail-first test: the control writes pageSize and the PDF comes out Letter-sized. Also check JSON Resume/Backup keep pageSize through export → import (tests/unit/page-size.unit.mjs exists — read it).

Make '1-Page Fit' (DesignPanel.jsx ~162-200 page-fit presets) actually fit: after applying its tight settings, measure the real page count with the app's own PDF renderer (the same react-pdf path the preview/export use; find how the app counts pages) and, while it is still more than one page, step down a fixed ladder of tighter settings that stays inside the panel's own min ranges (margins, section/entry spacing, line height, then font size), stopping at the FIRST step that fits — never tighter than needed. If even the tightest step is still over one page, keep the tightest and tell the user in the panel (role=status text, e.g. 'Still 2 pages at the tightest spacing — shorten the content to fit one page'). Never change content. Show a busy state while measuring and ignore double clicks; Balanced and Spacious stay as they are. Put the fit loop in a small module with the page counter injectable, so a tests/pdf/91- test drives it with the PDF harness: a 3-page fictional fixture → either 1 page or the notice; a fixture that fits at step N gets exactly step N. The Cypress spec 30-starters-and-design.cy.js clicks 1-Page Fit and checks the store/margin — keep it passing (run it on CI).

Tests only (a fix commit with fail-first only if a test exposes a real bug). Cover on the real components over the fake DOM (tests/pdf/fake-dom.mjs / tests/unit/ui-dom-harness.mjs; see how tests/pdf/parity/panels.mjs and walker.mjs already mount the Design panels): DesignPanel resetSection (each section's Reset restores that section's defaults and leaves every other setting alone), the page-fit presets (the values Balanced and Spacious write, and 1-Page Fit's result — R2-149's module was built just before you, don't duplicate its tests), the contact icon size control, DesignPanelTypography custom font add/remove (DesignPanelTypography.jsx ~27-50), setBase delta keeping (~56-64: changing the base size keeps each level's delta), Small/Normal/Large (~111-117), HeaderIconPickerModal (open, pick an icon → written to the contact, search/filter if any, close/cancel writes nothing), StarterTemplateModal (pick a starter → applied/created as the app does, cancel does nothing). First grep tests/ (parity walkers, 15-design-defaults, starter-templates.unit, contact-icon tests) and cover only what isn't pinned yet — list in your summary what you found already covered.

Header spacing, the owner's own ask ('i want to have custom spacing between header items name and title … user can adjust space'). The engine has 13 clamped gap keys (src/constants/headerSpacing.js); 7 have UI rows (src/utils/headerSpacingRows.js). Give the other 6 a row in Personal Info → Header spacing: summaryGap (contacts ↔ summary / gap above the summary), headerGapBelow (header ↔ first section), headerRuleGap (text ↔ header border), headerPadY and headerPadX (banner/header padding), contactsSideGap. Show each row only on templates where that key moves something (follow how the existing 7 rows decide per template). Wire each key into every template that draws that gap — replace Modern's and Sidebar's hard-coded gaps (src/templates/pdf/ModernTemplatePDF.jsx ~79-82, ~103; SidebarTemplatePDF.jsx ~204) and any others with the engine key, keeping today's default value exactly when the key is unset, and do the same in the cover-letter letterhead and in Word where they draw the same gap. Each new row gets a parity measure (tests/pdf/parity/registry-header.mjs, 21-header-gaps.test.mjs) that fails if the control does nothing, and the default print must not move on any template (compare geometry at default). Fail-first: a test that sets each new key and sees the PDF move.

Typography gaps. Required core: (1) the offline / failed web-font fallback is no longer silent (src/templates/pdf/shared/pdfFontLoader.js ~218-225): when a chosen font can't be loaded and the PDF falls back to Noto Sans, the editor shows a visible notice naming the font (e.g. near the preview or in Design → Typography: 'Lora could not be loaded — the PDF uses Noto Sans until you are back online'), and it clears once the font loads; the export uses the same fallback consistently. (2) a heading letter-spacing control (Design → Typography or Headings) honoured by the PDF (section headings) and Word (w:spacing on the heading run); (3) a job-title size control (the header's job title under the name) honoured by the PDF (every template and the letterhead where it prints the job title) and Word. Then, only if all that is done and green, a separate name font. Per-section font → remaining. Each new control goes in the parity registry with a measure; unset, every template prints exactly as today (PdfSection.jsx ~24 and DesignPanelTypography.jsx ~144-148 are the starting points). Fail-first tests for each.

Read docs/tracking/templates-ui-suggestions.md (§2, §5) and templates-ui-bugs.md (TUI-* — check which are already fixed; don't redo them). Build: A13 description contrast (text-gray-400 → text-gray-600, 11px, DesignPanel.jsx ~66, ~82-84, ~87); A7 label the Design button at every width + min-h-11 min-w-11 + aria-pressed (EditorHeader.jsx ~107-113; KEEP its title attribute — three Cypress specs select by it); A8 role=radiogroup + role=radio/aria-checked + a visible 'Selected' marker on the template cards and on SegmentControl (DesignPanelShared.jsx); A11 data-testid='template-card' on each card and ≥44 px SegmentControl targets (~93); A14 aria-expanded + aria-controls on DesignSection (DesignPanelShared.jsx ~107-117, useId already imported). Fail-first tests over the fake DOM (roles/aria state follow the selection, the testid exists per template, contrast class). Run the Cypress specs that select templates or the Design button (grep cypress/e2e for 'Design', template names, 04-design.cy.js) and the a11y spec 21-a11y.cy.js on CI; update a spec only where it selects by something you intentionally changed.

rows.task: one atsRating, honest badges, switch copy, name on card
rows.brief: A10: one atsRating(template, settings) read by both the picker's ATS badge (TEMPLATE_PICKER / constants/templates.js ~61) and atsChecker (atsChecker.js ~589 reads the raw id — normalise through templateId()); re-pin tests/pdf/15-design-defaults.test.mjs ~150 to the derived set, not a literal. Then A6: honest badges and one-line descriptions derived from it and from what each engine really draws (e.g. Classic's 'Two-column header' is false; Executive's role-first inline entries; Sidebar's two modes — the badge must match the app's own ATS Check in both modes). A5: a correct 'Switching keeps … and changes …' line under the picker, derived from what setTemplate (useResumeStore.js ~237-243) really changes (headingStyle, sectionTitleCase, possibly name/job-title colours, per-template resolved textColor/titleOrder/header border/spacing). C2: each dashboard ResumeCard (src/components/ResumeCard.jsx ~30-50, ~88-89) shows its template's name. Fail-first tests: the picker badge equals the checker's verdict for every template × Sidebar mode; the card shows the name. Run the affected Cypress specs on CI (they may select by old descriptions — update only what you intentionally changed). Remaining for the row, report it: A1 thumbnails, A2 gallery dialog, A3 filter chips, A4 undo, A9 two Sidebar picker entries, A12, B3 categories, C1 page-1 card image, D1, E1 phone sheet, F1 letterhead thumbnail — unless one is trivially done along the way.

'I need templates, at least 10 variations' (owner). Ship B1 design presets: at least 5 named looks, so Design → Template lists ≥ 10 choices, each over an existing engine = a template id + a settings bundle (font family, colours, heading style, header alignment/layout, spacing, date style …) chosen so each is visibly distinct from its engine and from the others. Read templates-ui-suggestions.md §3 first: do NOT write into section.settings (entry layout stays per-template); a preset must never leave a header/name colour unreadable on its ground (TUI-1 — check how that was fixed); every preset enters the ATS battery (tests/pdf/42-ats-fields.test.mjs enumerates TEMPLATE_IDS and finds fixtures by template — make it walk the presets too) and must pass on every reader; the picker badge (atsRating, built just before you) rates a preset through its engine + settings. Applying a preset goes through the store like setTemplate (plus its settings patch) and records the preset id in settings so the picker marks it selected; switching to a plain template clears it; JSON Resume / Backup keep it. Put the presets in one table (e.g. src/constants/templatePresets.js) with a unit test pinning ids unique, engine valid, every setting key known to the parity registry / clamp ranges. PDF, Word, Markdown and ATS text follow automatically through settings — verify Word for a couple of presets. Remaining: B2 new layout code (the 10 designed layouts), B4 save-my-design.

Per-section styling, part 1: a bullet-marker choice for rich-text lists — bullet •, dash –, circle ◦, none. Decide the scope after reading the code: a Design-level setting (Design → e.g. Section/Entries area) unless a per-section option in Section Options is equally cheap and consistent with how other per-section styles work. Honoured by the PDF (src/utils/richText.js ~186, PdfRichText), Word (the docx numbering level text / bullet glyph), and the ATS plain text only if the ATS text mirrors the PDF's marker today (check tests/pdf/65-ats-text-parity and the ATS exporter; ATS-safe markers matter — keep what the battery accepts); Markdown keeps '-' list syntax. The legacy bullets[] path too. Unset = today's marker exactly. Parity registry entry + measure (the drawn glyph changes). Fail-first test.

Per-section styling, part 2: a pipe separator ('|') for Skills where the separator choices live (SectionEditorCustomizer.jsx ~104, ~113; PdfSectionsOne.jsx ~110; PdfSidebarSkills.jsx ~50 — read what separators exist today, e.g. comma / bullet), honoured by the PDF (main column and Sidebar), Word, Markdown and ATS text the same way the existing separators are. Unset = unchanged. Parity registry entry + measure; fail-first test. Also check Languages/Interests if they share the same separator control.

Per-section styling, part 3: an optional page-number footer ('Page 1 of 2', off by default) — a Design setting (put the control in its own small row/section: the design-page cluster is adding a Page size control to DesignPanel.jsx in parallel, so keep your hunk separate from theirs), honoured by the résumé PDF on every template (react-pdf fixed element with render={({pageNumber,totalPages})}, placed inside the bottom margin so it never overlaps content or changes pagination) and Word (docx footer with PageNumber.CURRENT / TOTAL_PAGES); not in the ATS text or Markdown; not on the cover letter unless trivial. Default off = every page prints exactly as today. Parity registry entry + measure (the footer text appears on each page); fail-first test. Remaining for the whole row R2-147 (report it on this task): section-heading icons, link styling, language/skill level visuals, grouped roles at one employer, column layout, photo greyscale and position.

The row's last gap: src/components/job/NotesTab.jsx (a RichTextEditor over contenteditable) has no test. Add a fake-dom test on the real component (tests/pdf/fake-dom.mjs; see tests/pdf/81-job-tracker-ui.test.mjs and 82-job-pipeline-tasks.test.mjs for how job components are mounted): existing notes render, typing/formatting writes the job's notes through the job store, clearing works, and whatever else NotesTab does (toolbar buttons, empty state). If the fake DOM lacks contenteditable/selection pieces, extend it minimally without breaking its other users. Tests only — a fix commit with fail-first only if the test exposes a real bug.

Jobs sync + an honest Privacy page. Read how résumés sync first: src/utils/cloudSync*.js, syncMerge.js, src/hooks/useCloudSync.js, useResumeSyncActions.js, docs/knowledge/05-state-auth-sync.md, firestore.rules, tests/pdf/18-cloud-sync-* and tests/pdf/fake-firestore.mjs. Core: when signed in, the Job Tracker's jobs sync to Firestore — per user (e.g. users/{uid}/jobs/{jobId}, one doc per job), per-job last-writer-wins by updatedAt with deletions kept (tombstones or the résumés' deletion mechanism, so a deleted job doesn't come back), a first-sync merge of local + remote where nothing is lost, a debounced push of local changes, offline tolerant with retry, a size guard like cloudSyncHeld — reusing the résumé sync modules where they generalise rather than copying them. Update firestore.rules for the new path (say in notes that the owner must deploy the rules). Tests against fake-firestore mirroring 18-cloud-sync-*: two devices converge, delete propagates, offline edits push later, sign-out stops sync. The Privacy page (src/pages/PrivacyPage.jsx ~50, ~61) must say exactly what syncs (and that boards are local until R2-140 lands — the next worker updates it). If the full engine can't be done safely in this task, ship the honest Privacy text plus jobs (and boards) in the Backup file if they aren't there already, and report sync as remaining.

Boards sync (docs/tracking/boards-plan.md Phase 3: boardSyncIo / boardSyncMerge (per-board LWW) / boardSyncEngine (first sync + debounced queue + offline/retry + size guard) / useBoardSync, wired into App.jsx) — build it on the engine the jobs sync (R2-145, done just before you on this branch) introduced, sharing code rather than a third copy. Per user, one doc per board (boards can be big: respect Firestore's 1 MiB doc cap — hold an over-cap board out of sync with a notice, like cloudSyncHeld). firestore.rules updated. Phase 4 tests: store/normaliser/ops tests mostly exist (tests/unit/board-*.unit.mjs, normalize-board.unit.mjs) — add the sync ones against fake-firestore (two devices converge, delete propagates, over-cap board is held, sign-out stops). Update the Privacy page so it says boards sync too. If R2-145 shipped only the fallback, do the same fallback for boards and report sync as remaining.

Tests only (a fix commit with fail-first only if a test exposes a real bug). The gate has no test of the section/entry structure actions on the real components: add a section, rename a section, hide/show a section, delete a section (with its confirm), add/delete an entry, reorder sections and entries by the drag handlers (src/components/EditorResumeTab.jsx ~28-35 handleSectionDragEnd → updateSections(arrayMove); src/components/SectionEditor.jsx ~46-51 handleItemDragEnd → reorderItems) and by keyboard (the sections cluster added keyboard reorder for entries — git log --grep keyboard), plus useResumeStore createResume / duplicateResume / renameResume / keepResume (src/hooks/useResumeSectionActions.js ~40-73, useResumeStore.js). tests/pdf/parity/40-structure.test.mjs already pins section and entry reorder through the store's drag actions — grep and don't duplicate; drive the components' own handlers over the fake DOM (tests/pdf/fake-dom.mjs, see 88-duplicate.test.mjs from the sections cluster) where the gap is, and check the result reaches the PDF where cheap. Summarise which regression each test catches.

Tests only (fix + fail-first only if a test finds a bug). Dashboard create, duplicate, rename, delete and import are tested only in Cypress (cypress/e2e/01-dashboard.cy.js). Add node-gate tests on the real Dashboard / ResumeCard components over the fake DOM with the real store (src/pages/Dashboard.jsx, src/components/ResumeCard.jsx, src/hooks/useResumeStore.js ~153-197): New Résumé (and the starter picker's path), duplicate (a deep copy with fresh ids, placed as the app places it), rename (inline rename commits/escapes), delete (confirm → gone; cancel → kept; the local-deletions record if the store keeps one), import (a JSON Resume / backup file through the dashboard's import control). Don't duplicate tests R2-158 wrote just before you.

Tests only (fix + fail-first only if a test finds a bug). The export half is already covered (70-markdown-parity, 65-ats-text-parity, json-resume-sections / json-resume-reprint). Do the editor half: section visibility (hide → the PDF, Word, Markdown and ATS text all omit it; show → back), section delete reaching the exporters, MonthPicker writes (picking a month and a year writes the date string the exporters read; clear; the 'Present'/current interplay — tests/pdf/30-date-editor.test.mjs only covers display), and the Sidebar's single-column section resolution (tests/pdf/10-section-options.test.mjs has no sidebarSingleColumn case: with Single · ATS-safe Layout on, which sections go where, on every relevant section type). Don't duplicate what R2-158 / R2-167 just wrote on this branch.

The ATS checker's claims are unproven, it misses risky layouts, and there is no 'what a parser reads' view or per-field scoring (src/components/AtsCheckerPanel.jsx ~208; src/utils/atsChecker.js ~1073-1074; tests/pdf/ats-fields.mjs ~210). First confirm at HEAD: the ats cluster (R2-020…027, 078…081, 163, 166) changed the checker — tests/unit/ats-section-grids.unit.mjs may already make Grids 2 lower the layout score; if so record the proof. Core: (1) the layout check covers every layout the app can produce that its own battery shows parsing badly (section Grids > 1, the two-column Sidebar vs its Single · ATS-safe mode, contacts in columns, icon-only contacts, text inside the banner…), and each claim the panel states is pinned by a test that compares it with what the battery (tests/pdf/ats-*.mjs, pdftotext/pdf.js readers) actually gets from the app's PDF — fix any claim that the battery contradicts; (2) a 'What a parser reads' view in the ATS tab: the plain text extracted from the actual PDF with pdf.js (pdfjs-dist is already a dependency and the preview uses it) in reading order, collapsible, with Copy — so users see what an ATS sees, and it agrees with the ATS text export where the PDF does; (3) per-field scoring if (1) and (2) are done and green: for each Experience entry, whether title, company, dates and location come out as separable lines in that text, shown per entry. Fail-first tests for each fix; fake-dom tests for the panel. Run tests/pdf/77-ats-panel.test.mjs, 56-, 58-, 65-, 42-ats-fields and tests/unit/ats-*.unit.mjs on CI, and cypress/e2e/27-ats-checker.cy.js. Remaining: whatever of (3) isn't done.

One letter per résumé; 'New Cover Letter' creates a blank résumé with no name or contacts, listed as a résumé (src/pages/Dashboard.jsx ~121, ~217; src/hooks/useResumeStore.js ~259). Read how cover letters are modelled today (the letter cluster R2-043…134 changed them: git log --grep letter) and docs/knowledge. Core: New Cover Letter creates a letter pre-filled with the name, job title, contacts (and the photo setting) of a résumé — the most recently edited one, or a small picker when there are several (and a blank letter when there are none); the dashboard lists letters as letters (their own group or a clear 'Cover letter' label/filter), never counted or shown as a résumé; several letters can exist and each can be opened, renamed, duplicated and deleted like a résumé. Existing stored 'Cover Letter' résumés keep loading and printing the same (a migration if the data shape changes, with a test on old data). Check the letter's PDF, Word and text exports read the pre-filled data. Fail-first tests (store + fake-dom Dashboard); run cypress/e2e specs touching the dashboard and letters on CI (grep 'Cover Letter'). Remaining: a live link from a letter to its résumé so later edits to the résumé's contacts propagate, if you don't build it.

'Beyond design': the Import menu accepts only JSON (src/components/ImportMenu.jsx ~39). Core: import a résumé from PDF, DOCX and plain text / Markdown. Extract the text (PDF via pdfjs-dist, already a dependency — reuse how the preview loads it; DOCX by unzipping word/document.xml — check whether jszip is already installed as a dependency of docx: if you import it directly, declare it in package.json via yarn; text/Markdown read directly), then parse into a new résumé: name, job title, contacts (email, phone, links, location), summary, and sections split by known headings (Experience, Education, Skills, Projects, Languages, Certifications … and the app's own heading names), entries best-effort (title / company / date-range lines for Experience and Education); nothing is lost — any text not placed lands in a custom section. Put the parser in a pure module with unit tests. Key test: round-trip the app's own PDF, Word, Markdown and ATS-text exports of a fictional fixture (tests/pdf/harness.mjs renders the PDF) back through the importer and check name, contacts, section headings and entry titles/dates come back. The import UI tells the user it is a best-effort import to review. Then, only if that is done and green, résumé language for dates (month names and 'Present' via a settings language honoured by every exporter through src/utils/dates.js ~44-46). Remaining (report): language/RTL (whatever isn't done), public web link, several cover letters per résumé (say what R2-135 covered).

Repo housekeeping. TODO_RESOLVE_CONFLICTS.md is already gone at HEAD (find the deleting commit: git log --diff-filter=D --oneline -- TODO_RESOLVE_CONFLICTS.md). Fix the stale knowledge docs under docs/knowledge/ (allowed — only docs/tracking/ is off-limits): old /home/sairam/... paths, the DATA_VERSION in 05-state-auth-sync.md vs src/utils/dataVersion.js, 06-templates-export.md ~23-25, and anything that predates per-résumé migrations — check each claim against src/. graphify-out/ is generated output and stale (names the deleted CareerTimeline.jsx): check nothing reads it (grep), then stop tracking it (git rm -r --cached graphify-out + a .gitignore line) — the files stay on disk. D5, now ordered by the owner: declare @napi-rs/canvas as a devDependency (tests/pdf/11-photo*.test.mjs skip without it — they will start running on CI, so dispatch them and make them pass; if a skipped test was hiding a real bug, fix it with fail-first), and drop file-saver if nothing imports it (grep src tests cypress). Use yarn for package.json/yarn.lock (follow the RULES' private node_modules steps). CI's fail-first undoes src/, .yarn/patches and yarn.lock only — a docs/deps change is proven by a dispatch that shows it.

Open-source release. LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING and part of the README landed in 12c2a71 (git show --stat 12c2a71). Finish: (1) README accurate against src/ — file map, template list, routes (job tracker, boards), scripts and test commands (tests run on CI; say how a contributor runs them), link docs/knowledge; (2) owner-specific defaults out of the source (src/utils/demoAccounts.js ~9, src/hooks/useAuth.js ~23, ~34 — personal emails / UIDs / names): move them to VITE_* env vars documented in .env.example (the owner's own deployment keeps working when the env is set; a fork gets neutral behaviour), and check vite-plugin-owner-resume.js and the demo seed — if the default seed is the owner's real résumé, a fork must get a neutral fictional placeholder (keep the owner's path through env); (3) the app works fully with no Firebase env (auth disabled gracefully) — verify by reading, add a unit test if cheap. Fail-first tests for src changes (e.g. with no env the demo accounts list is empty / neutral). Run the Cypress demo-account specs (cypress/e2e/11-demo-account*.cy.js) and any tests reading demoAccounts/useAuth on CI. Remaining (owner only): tag v0.1.0 (this session may not push tags), confirming Terms/Privacy match the hosting domain.

The old push gate (pushgate.sh, outside the repo) is superseded by .github/workflows/ci.yml (commit e6796ec added lint and Cypress; later commits added sharding and the dispatch inputs). Verify each claim of the row against ci.yml at HEAD: a failing node test fails its job (bash -eo pipefail with tee), a failing build fails, browser suites and lint run on master pushes and full dispatches, and whether skipped tests are hidden — the summaries print '# skipped' but nothing flags them: if tests are skipped in a full run, emit a ::warning:: with the count and names (not a failure — some skips are deliberate, e.g. 11-photo without @napi-rs/canvas). Fix any real gap in ci.yml minimally without changing the dispatch inputs' behaviour (the coordinator and nine other clusters rely on them). Prove a ci.yml change with a dispatch whose logs show it. If nothing real is left, outcome already-fixed with the proof (file:line in ci.yml).

Process/tracking. Push-gate half: the hardening that lived as an uncommitted change in the owner's memory store is superseded by CI (R2-154, done just before you) — say so with proof. Tracking-docs half: PENDING-ALL.md ~17-23, ~31-37 and templates-ui-plan.md ~188-194 are under docs/tracking/, which ONLY the coordinator edits: do not edit them; instead put in notes exactly which lines are stale and what they should say now (check each against HEAD). Check whether branch templates-ui-audit / commit 45f4acc exists on origin (git ls-remote origin; git cat-file -e 45f4acc) and whether its content is on the work branch. Outcome: partial or already-fixed as the proof allows, with the tracker edits handed to the coordinator.
